principles.text: Sell it manually before you code. Real payment is the validation, not polite interest.
Target leads showing intent today instead of static lists; it gets two to five times more replies.
Offer a free blueprint instead of asking for a demo; saying yes to it is far easier.
Each stage needs a different channel; move on once you have mastered one or hit its ceiling.
On Reddit, entertain with stories and proof; keep your product out of the post body.

sampleQA.question: I have a B2B SaaS idea. What should I do before writing code?

answer.text: Make a simple deck (his first was 6 ugly slides) and pitch it to your ICP. If they ask the price or agree to buy, there is something.
Get paid first and deliver the result by hand; Gojiberry sold manually found leads before building the product.
For the first 10 customers, get 20 to 30 meetings and close ten. Start pricing by matching competitors who already sell.

sampleQA.question: How do I get replies on cold outreach?

answer.text: Fix the lead source first: cold email fails mostly from stale lists, so email people with fresh intent signals.
On LinkedIn, contact people active in the last 24 to 48 hours; that alone roughly doubles response.
Ask permission to send a blueprint rather than pushing a demo, so replying takes almost no thought.
Let AI source and draft, but have a human take over once a prospect replies.

sampleQA.question: How do I use Reddit for my SaaS without getting banned?

answer.text: Warm up a new account for 7 to 14 days with comments and upvotes; get at least 10 karma before mentioning your SaaS.
Write story posts with proof and keep the product out of the body; name it and link only when someone asks.
Aim for about 10 upvotes in the first 10 minutes and reply to every comment.
